admission.workflow: Activate one immutable Proctor window composition and provide lifecycle, shell parts, bounded layout, item groups, cancellable pane resolution, safe restoration, and modal or gate mechanics without importing VS Code product aggregates.

items.rationale: Canonical Microsoft MIT text for the reviewed workbench evidence.
Retain monotonic startup phases, limited early blockers, ordered activation, and eventual work without carrying VS Code service aggregates.
Retain typed item identity, presentation, capabilities, groups, history, view state, and resolver seams under Proctor WorkbenchItem terminology.
Retain identity matching and presentation-change behavior while excluding local resource and capability assumptions.
Retain one-time pane creation, cancellable assignment, clearing, visibility, layout, focus, view state, and disposal.
Retain identity deduplication, active-item history, close capability, bounded groups, and controlled splits.
Retain structural workbench parts and coordinated layout while permitting only composition-approved placements and sizes.
Retain bounded pointer and keyboard resizing, separator semantics, values, and reset without exposing a generic docking surface.
Arbitrary grid mutation conflicts with immutable Proctor shell topology; the required size propagation and bounded splits are retained through the composition policy.
Its constraint, sash, and layout invariants inform the bounded shell implementation; generic add, move, swap, distribute, and snap APIs are not product boundaries.
The aggregate VS Code workbench selects unrelated product services and contributions; three Proctor code entrypoints import only their exact literal manifests.
Pane visibility, focus, layout and lifecycle semantics are retained without VS Code view-container and extension registration assumptions.

dependencies.rationale: The admitted event, cancellation and disposal primitives own deterministic lifecycle.
Shell and overlay CSS consume Proctor semantic variables only.
Privileged main-process window identity remains separate from renderer composition.

divergences.summary: Authenticated and Candidate renderer entrypoints statically import distinct literal workbench manifests and exact executable registrations; remote projections and restoration can create only authorized instances of packaged types.
Restoration is bounded to admitted packaged item types and recursively rejects malformed, oversized, or security-sensitive state; Candidate is never a restorable application entrypoint.

The fixed shell provides only approved regions, at most four internal groups, accessible separators and command-routed reset, exact direct-body viewport ownership, with no arbitrary docking or detached windows.

verification.obligation: Verify composition validation/freezing, lifecycle ordering and failure isolation, item group/history rules, split bounds, and restoration filtering.
Verify all Candidate shell regions, keyboard resizing/reset, modal inertness/action/focus restoration, stale item fencing, model disposal, and renderer sandboxing in real Chromium.
Verify every production code entrypoint is reachable from one declared composition and cannot reach forbidden roots or undeclared dynamic modules.
Verify layer direction, cycle absence, one stylesheet owner/root, accepted cascade, and Proctor custom-property ownership.
Verify every reviewed workbench evidence blob at the exact pinned VS Code revision.
